verdict.reasoning: Patient states, "diarrhoea... it's lasting for like three days."
Patient says, "I can't go to work because I need to go... when I finish, I feel I need to go again... I need to be like close to the toilet uh, all the time."
Patient reports a sense of incomplete evacuation: "I go to the toilet, and then when I finish, I need to, I feel I need to go again."

Location: "the pain is mainly focus in, in the centre area of the abdomen, like under the belly button." Non-radiating and relieved by bowel movements: "No, no, just there, and it seems to be alleviate a bit, toilet."
Patient notes audible abdominal sounds: "sometimes I can hear my stomach, uh, like, it comes, uh, yeah."
Sequence: had fruit then nausea and vomiting—"I had some fruit... And afterwards, I didn't have anything, then I got a bit of nausea, and I vomited." Timing: "I think it was this morning."
Patient denies hematemesis and attributes red color to strawberries: "I don't think there is blood because... it was the strawberries that I was having for breakfast. So... it wasn't blood."
When asked about blood, patient says, "Uh, no, I haven't noticed any, any blood" referring to diarrhea/stool.
Decreased intake: "I try not to eat a lot because I... going to the toilet every ten minute." Low fluids: "I think I don't drink enough water."
Patient: "I didn't have any, fever recently... I was sweating a little bit the last four days, but I... don't think so, I don't think" (re fever).

Baseline asthma: "I have, I have, I have a, asthma." No increase in SOB: "apart of the normal, I haven't, I haven't" when asked about breathing. No chest pain: "no, I haven't, I haven't noticed any chest pain."
Work impact: "I can't go to work because I need to go..." Functional status: "walking and talking, uh, yes, yes" though staying home due to toilet needs.
Patient clearly states: "I have, I have, I have a, asthma."
Patient uses inhaler and changed brand: "I take some... inhaler" and later "my inhaler kind of run out... I have this brand, but I bought a new one here... maybe this new one has cause it."
Patient: "I have an allergy. I have N, N, NK, NKDA allergy." NKDA denotes no known drug allergies.
Patient: "my father... died about um, ten years ago of bowel cancer."
Patient indicates staying home: "I don't walk very far because... I need to go to the toilet... So, I'm spending some time at home." Doctor also advises, "please stay home for the time being."

Self-palpation tenderness: Doctor asks, "when you press on your tummy, does it cause any pain?" Patient: "Ohh, it does a little bit." Location earlier specified as "centre area of the abdomen, like under the belly button."

Doctor impression: "you might have eaten something bad, and it's causing your tummy pain... this is normally called gastroenteritis." 3 days non-bloody diarrhea, infra-umbilical pain, N/V, decreased intake, and no clear fever are all documented in prior quotes.

Mild tenderness: "when you press on your tummy... Ohh, it does a little bit." Infectious/foodborne cause: Doctor—"you might have eaten something bad... this is normally called gastroenteritis, so, an infection of the tummy."
Anxiety due to family history: patient is worried about father's bowel cancer. Doctor: "most suggestive of an infection of your tummy and less likely to be something your father had."
Doctor advises increased fluids: "Number one is to drink lots of water and fluids, because you're losing lots at the moment."
Rest at home/off work: "please stay home for the time being until you get slightly better"; patient already not going to work due to symptoms.
Doctor: "Number two is to make sure and look out for any fevers, so, if you start getting a temperature then you need..." indicating monitoring for fever.
Doctor: "Normally, things like antibiotics don't help, they make the situation worse." This is an instruction to avoid antibiotics.
Doctor: "if you feel you're getting much worse, than I would suggest you go and see your GP in real, in real life, in person, so they can look at your belly."

Reassurance re cancer: "most suggestive of an infection of your tummy and less likely to be something your father had" and "if your things don't get worse, then that's something that we can look up from the GP" (re discussing cancer risk with GP).
